
SHOW-COVERAGE
Display coverage report showing scenario-to-test-to-implementation traceability

WHEN TO USE
  Use this command to view coverage status for features, identify uncovered scenarios (gaps), verify traceability links, and track reverse ACDD mapping progress. Run regularly to find scenarios that need test/implementation links.

USAGE
  fspec show-coverage [feature-name] [options]

ARGUMENTS
  [feature-name] (optional)
    Feature file name (without path or extension), e.g., "user-authentication". If omitted, shows project-wide coverage.

OPTIONS
  --format <format>
    Output format: text or json (default: text)
  --output <file>
    Write output to file instead of stdout

COMMON PATTERNS
  • Find Coverage Gaps
    Example: # See project-wide coverage
fspec show-coverage

# Focus on specific feature
fspec show-coverage user-authentication

# Identify scenarios marked ❌ NOT COVERED
# Link missing tests/implementation
    undefined

  • Reverse ACDD Progress Tracking
    Example: # Check what percentage of scenarios are mapped
fspec show-coverage
# Output: Overall Coverage: 20% (4/20 scenarios)

# Map more scenarios...
fspec link-coverage ...

# Check progress
fspec show-coverage
# Output: Overall Coverage: 45% (9/20 scenarios)
    undefined

  • Export Coverage for CI/CD
    Example: # Export as JSON for automated checks
fspec show-coverage --format=json --output=coverage.json

# Parse in CI pipeline to enforce coverage thresholds
jq '.coveragePercent' coverage.json
    undefined


TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  1. fspec show-coverage → 2. Identify uncovered scenarios (gaps) → 3. Link tests/implementation → 4. Verify coverage increased

EXAMPLES
  1. Show coverage for specific feature
  $ fspec show-coverage user-authentication
  Coverage Report: user-authentication.feature
Coverage: 50% (1/2 scenarios)

## Scenarios
### ✅ Login with valid credentials (FULLY COVERED)
- **Test**: src/__tests__/auth.test.ts:45-62
- **Implementation**: src/auth/login.ts:10,11,12,23,24

### ❌ Login with invalid credentials (NOT COVERED)
- No test mappings

  2. Show project-wide coverage report
  $ fspec show-coverage
  Project Coverage Report
Overall Coverage: 65% (13/20 scenarios)

Features Overview:
- user-authentication.feature: 50% (1/2) ⚠️
- user-logout.feature: 100% (1/1) ✅
- dashboard.feature: 67% (2/3) ⚠️
- admin-tools.feature: 100% (4/4) ✅

  3. Get coverage in JSON format for programmatic access
  $ fspec show-coverage user-authentication --format=json
  {
  "feature": "user-authentication",
  "totalScenarios": 2,
  "coveredScenarios": 1,
  "coveragePercent": 50,
  "scenarios": [...]
}

  4. Save coverage report to file
  $ fspec show-coverage --output=coverage-report.txt
  ✓ Coverage report written to coverage-report.txt

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Error: Feature file user-authentication.feature not found
    Fix: Check feature name matches file name. Run: fspec list-features

  ✗ Error: Coverage file user-authentication.feature.coverage not found
    Fix: Coverage file should auto-create with fspec create-feature. Try running create-feature again.

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec link-coverage
  fspec audit-coverage
  fspec unlink-coverage
  fspec list-features

NOTES
  • Coverage symbols: ✅ FULLY COVERED, ⚠️ PARTIALLY COVERED (test only), ❌ NOT COVERED
  • Project-wide report (no args) shows overall coverage percentage
  • Use --format=json for programmatic access in CI/CD pipelines
  • Coverage percentages based on scenarios, not lines of code
  • Run regularly to track reverse ACDD mapping progress
